scope: Numbers 13–18, all 214 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 13–15, 16:1–35 and 18 align directly. Public 16:36–50 maps to Hebrew 17:1–15; public 17:1–13 maps to Hebrew 17:16–28. All 214 original records, including every annotation, are hashed exactly. Later numbering differences require separate mapping.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Introduces the divine commission as speech continued into verse 2; no additional commissioning agent.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Scouting renders tur without importing espionage; keeps one man per ancestral tribe and the divine gift.
verses.before: “Send men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe send one man, each person a leader among them.”
verses.after: “Send men to scout the land of Canaan, which I am giving the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each a leader among his people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Send men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each ancestral tribe send one man, each one a leader among them.”

verses.rationale: Unpacks mouth-command idiom and retains departure place and all men’s leadership.
verses.before: So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the command of the LORD. All of them were men who were heads among the Israelites.
verses.after: At the LORD’s command, Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran. Every man was a leader of the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran according to the command of the LORD. All of them were men who were heads among the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Begins a connected list with explicit tribal representation; retains Shammua and Zaccur.
verses.before: These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
verses.after: These were their names. Reuben’s tribe sent Shammua son of Zaccur;
verses.tsw_comparator: These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;

verses.rationale: Parallel list syntax retains Simeon, Shaphat and Hori without changing names for difference.
verses.before: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
verses.after: Simeon’s tribe, Shaphat son of Hori;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;

verses.rationale: Retains Caleb’s tribal and paternal identification for his later speech.
verses.before: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
verses.after: Judah’s tribe, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

verses.rationale: Preserves Igal and his father Joseph, distinct from the tribal Joseph in verse 11.
verses.before: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
verses.after: Issachar’s tribe, Igal son of Joseph;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;

verses.rationale: Keeps Hoshea here so verse 16’s naming notice remains visible; no premature harmonization to Joshua.
verses.before: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
verses.after: Ephraim’s tribe, Hoshea son of Nun;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;

verses.rationale: Maintains Palti’s father and tribe in the continuous list.
verses.before: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
verses.after: Benjamin’s tribe, Palti son of Raphu;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;

verses.rationale: Preserves the full Gaddiel name, distinct from Gaddi in the next verse.
verses.before: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
verses.after: Zebulun’s tribe, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;

verses.rationale: Retains both tribal designations and clarifies their apposition without emending the Hebrew.
verses.before: from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
verses.after: Joseph’s tribe—that is, Manasseh’s tribe—Gaddi son of Susi;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;

verses.rationale: Keeps the Dan representative and patronymic in list order.
verses.before: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
verses.after: Dan’s tribe, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;

verses.rationale: Retains Sethur and Michael without modernizing biblical proper names.
verses.before: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
verses.after: Asher’s tribe, Sethur son of Michael;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;

verses.rationale: Maintains Nahbi and Vophsi in the same tribal sequence as the source.
verses.before: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
verses.after: Naphtali’s tribe, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;

verses.rationale: Closes the twelve-man list with Gad rather than reordering it to earlier census lists.
verses.before: from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
verses.after: and Gad’s tribe, Geuel son of Machi.
verses.tsw_comparator: from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.

verses.rationale: Separates list conclusion and naming action; does not assert when the naming first happened.
verses.before: These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
verses.after: Those were the men Moses sent to scout the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.

verses.rationale: Makes route instructions audible, retaining ascent and both terrain designations.
verses.before: Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan and said to them, “Go up through the Negev and then go up into the hill country.
verses.after: When Moses sent them to scout Canaan, he told them, “Go up this way through the Negev, then into the hill country.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan and said to them, “Go up through the Negev and then go up into the hill country.

verses.rationale: Turns embedded alternatives into short questions without losing either contrast.
verses.before: See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many;
verses.after: Find out what the land is like. Are its people strong or weak? Are there few of them or many?
verses.tsw_comparator: See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many;

verses.rationale: Retains land quality and settlement defenses as separate scouting questions.
verses.before: whether the land in which they live is good or bad; whether the cities in which they live are camps or fortifications;
verses.after: Is the land they live in good or bad? What are their towns like—open camps or fortified places?
verses.tsw_comparator: whether the land in which they live is good or bad; whether the cities in which they live are camps or fortifications;

verses.rationale: Renders fat/lean soil idiom, keeps trees rather than assuming forests, and preserves seasonal aside.
verses.before: and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be courageous and take some of the fruit of the land.” Now the season was the season of the first ripe grapes.
verses.after: Is the soil rich or poor? Are there trees or not? Be courageous, and bring back some of the land’s fruit.” It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be courageous and take some of the fruit of the land.” Now the season was the season of the first ripe grapes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the southern and northern limits; treats Lebo-hamath as a place name with alternate reading noted.
verses.before: So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
verses.after: They went up and scouted the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.

verses.rationale: Collective English follows the expedition context; notes the singular Hebrew arrival verb without silently naming Caleb. Keeps seven-year comparison.
verses.before: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
verses.after: They went up through the Negev and reached Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were there. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves one cluster, two carriers, pole and all three fruits; divides actions for listening.
verses.before: They came to the Wadi Eshcol and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which two of them carried on a pole, along with some pomegranates and figs.
verses.after: At the Valley of Eshcol, they cut a branch with a single cluster of grapes. Two men carried it on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to the Wadi Eshcol and cut down from there a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which two of them carried on a pole, along with some pomegranates and figs.

verses.rationale: Uses passive naming for an unspecified subject and retains Eshcol/cluster connection for a vocabulary note.
verses.before: That place was called the Wadi Eshcol because of the cluster that the Israelites cut down from there.
verses.after: That place was named the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster the Israelites cut there.
verses.tsw_comparator: That place was called the Wadi Eshcol because of the cluster that the Israelites cut down from there.

verses.rationale: Foregrounds the exact forty days that becomes the judgment’s measure.
verses.before: At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.
verses.after: After forty days of scouting the land, they returned.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps both leaders and community as recipients and preserves report plus visible fruit.
verses.before: They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back word to them and to the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.
verses.after: They came to Moses, Aaron and the whole Israelite community at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They gave their report to them and the whole community, and showed them the land’s fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back word to them and to the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.

verses.rationale: Retains the familiar abundance image and demonstrative evidence as the speakers’ favorable opening.
verses.before: They reported to him and said, “We came to the land where you sent us. It truly flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
verses.after: They told Moses, “We went into the land you sent us to. It really does flow with milk and honey! Here is its fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: They reported to him and said, “We came to the land where you sent us. It truly flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.

verses.rationale: Gives the adversative full force without calling the report wholly false or adding measurements.
verses.before: Even so, the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.
verses.after: But the people living there are powerful, and their cities are fortified and very large. We even saw descendants of Anak there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.

verses.rationale: Keeps five peoples and their three geographic groupings distinct.
verses.before: Amalek lives in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
verses.after: Amalekites live in the Negev. Hittites, Jebusites and Amorites live in the hill country. Canaanites live beside the sea and along the Jordan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Amalek lives in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”

verses.rationale: Conveys both emphatic Hebrew constructions and the challenge to the other report in direct speech.
verses.before: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We should certainly go up and take possession of it, for we are surely able to overcome it.”
verses.after: Caleb quieted the people before Moses. “We must go up and take possession of it!” he said. “We certainly can!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We should certainly go up and take possession of it, for we are surely able to overcome it.”

verses.rationale: Retains the competing claim as the men’s speech; stronger-than-us is the contextual reading.
verses.before: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.”
verses.after: But the men who had gone with him said, “We cannot go up against these people. They are stronger than we are.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the devouring-land image and universal exaggeration as quoted report, not narrator-certified geography.
verses.before: So they brought to the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are people of great stature.
verses.after: They spread a bad report among the Israelites about the land they had scouted: “The land we went through to scout devours its inhabitants. Every person we saw there was huge.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they brought to the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw in it are people of great stature.

verses.rationale: Keeps Nephilim and the ancestry clause in the pinned Hebrew; preserves both perspectives as the scouts’ claim.
verses.before: There we saw the Nephilim—the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim—and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.”
verses.after: We saw the Nephilim there—the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim. In our own eyes we were like grasshoppers, and that is how we looked to them too.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There we saw the Nephilim—the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim—and we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.”

verses.rationale: Retains collective outcry and night-long narrative setting without adding a motive.
verses.before: Then the whole congregation raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept that night.
verses.after: The whole community cried out, and the people wept that night.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the whole congregation raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept that night.

verses.rationale: Keeps both leaders and repeated death wish, which the subsequent judgment answers.
verses.before: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
verses.after: All the Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron. The whole community said to them, “If only we had died in Egypt! If only we had died in this wilderness!
verses.tsw_comparator: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!

verses.rationale: Preserves lethal violence and the gender-specific wives and vulnerable little ones, retaining plunder’s dehumanizing image.
verses.before: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?”
verses.after: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and little ones will be taken as plunder. Wouldn’t we be better off going back to Egypt?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?”

verses.rationale: Renders head as leader and retains the concrete proposal, not merely an inward wish.
verses.before: And they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
verses.after: They said to one another, “Let’s choose a leader and go back to Egypt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”

verses.rationale: Retains visible bodily action without inventing a spoken prayer or a named addressee for the posture.
verses.before: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the congregation of the Israelites.
verses.after: Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the assembled Israelite community.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the congregation of the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Retains both men, fathers, participation and grief gesture.
verses.before: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among people who explored the land, tore their clothes
verses.after: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who had scouted the land, tore their clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who explored the land, tore their clothes

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled very instead of flattening the emphatic positive counter-report.
verses.before: and spoke to the whole congregation of the Israelites, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore is an exceedingly good land.
verses.after: They told the whole Israelite community, “The land we went through to scout is very, very good.
verses.tsw_comparator: and spoke to the whole congregation of the Israelites, saying, “The land through which we passed to explore is an exceedingly good land.

verses.rationale: Retains the condition, divine gift and repeated land image without changing it into an unconditional prediction.
verses.before: If the LORD delights in us, the LORD will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.after: If the LORD delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us. It is a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the LORD delights in us, the LORD will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.rationale: Preserves bread and shade metaphors, supported by a selective note, and both fear prohibitions.
verses.before: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their protection has departed from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them.”
verses.after: Only do not rebel against the LORD. Do not fear the people of the land—they are bread for us! Their shade has left them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not fear the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their protection has departed from them, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them.”

verses.rationale: Keeps threatened execution and the interrupting appearance; does not add the cloud from other witnesses.
verses.before: But the whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the Israelites.
verses.after: The whole community called for them to be stoned. Then the LORD’s glory appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the whole congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the Tent of Meeting to all the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Makes the repeated questions audible; trust conveys reliance rather than mere intellectual assent.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people despise me? How long will they refuse to trust me, in spite of all the signs I have done in their midst?
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “How long will these people despise me? How long will they refuse to trust me, despite all the signs I have done among them?
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people despise me? How long will they refuse to trust me, in spite of all the signs I have done in their midst?

verses.rationale: Keeps both plague and disinheritance and the comparison with the proposed nation from Moses.
verses.before: I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and I will make from you a nation greater and mightier than they.”
verses.after: I will strike them with plague and disinherit them. Then I will make you a greater and stronger nation than they are.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strike them with pestilence and dispossess them, and I will make from you a nation greater and mightier than they.”

verses.rationale: Connects the Egyptians’ hearing with the power displayed in the exodus across the verse boundary.
verses.before: Yet Moses said to the LORD, “Then Egypt will hear of it, for by your power you brought this people up from their midst,
verses.after: Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear about it. You brought these people out from among them by your power,
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said to the LORD, “Then Egypt will hear of it, for by your power you brought this people up from their midst,

verses.rationale: Keeps unusual eye-to-eye idiom rather than harmonizing mouth-to-mouth in chapter 12; retains each reported manifestation.
verses.before: and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, O LORD, are among this people; that you, O LORD, are seen face to face; that your cloud stands over them; and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
verses.after: and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, LORD, are among these people, that you, LORD, appear eye to eye, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go ahead of them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
verses.tsw_comparator: and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, O LORD, are in the midst of this people; that you, O LORD, are seen face to face; that your cloud stands over them; and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.

verses.rationale: Retains conditional killing of the collective as one and leads into the nations’ quotation.
verses.before: If you put this people to death as one person, then the nations who have heard of your fame will say,
verses.after: If you kill this people as one, the nations that have heard of you will say,
verses.tsw_comparator: If you put this people to death as one person, then the nations who have heard of your fame will say,

verses.rationale: Preserves the harsh slaughter verb and marks the statement as the imagined nations’ explanation.
verses.before: ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land sworn to them, the LORD slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
verses.after: ‘The LORD could not bring these people into the land he swore to give them, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land sworn to them, the LORD slaughtered them in the wilderness.’

verses.rationale: Distinguishes Adonai as my Lord from the divine name and retains the plea’s appeal to prior speech.
verses.before: And now, please, let the power of the Lord be great, just as you have spoken, saying,
verses.after: Now, please, let my Lord’s power be great, just as you said:
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, please, let the power of the Lord be great, just as you have spoken, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the clauses actually quoted from Exodus 34 with recognizable shared wording and poetic lineation. Retains intergenerational guilt without reducing it to natural consequences or importing omitted clauses.
verses.before: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, yet by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of parents upon children to the third and fourth generation.’
verses.after: ‘The LORD is slow to anger, abounding in faithful love, forgiving guilt and rebellion, yet certainly not clearing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ guilt upon their children, to the third and fourth generations.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, yet by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of parents upon children to the third and fourth generation.’

verses.rationale: Retains pardon petition and bearing idiom’s patient-support sense; the note acknowledges forgiving as alternate for nasa.
verses.before: Please forgive the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now.”
verses.after: Please forgive these people’s wrongdoing in keeping with your great faithful love, just as you have borne with them from Egypt until now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Please forgive the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now.”

verses.rationale: Keeps pardon explicit before judgment rather than interpreting the judgment as a refusal to forgive.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, “I have forgiven according to your word.
verses.after: The LORD replied, “I have forgiven them, as you asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, “I have forgiven according to your word.

verses.rationale: Reads the glory clause within the oath; note retains possible future will-be-filled construal.
verses.before: Even so, as I live, and as all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD,
verses.after: But as surely as I live, and as surely as the LORD’s glory fills the whole earth,
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, as I live, and as all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Preserves ten times, seen glory/signs and heard voice imagery; syntax continues to oath consequence.
verses.before: none of the people who have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice,
verses.after: all those who have seen my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and the wilderness, yet have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice—
verses.tsw_comparator: none of the people who have seen my glory and my signs that I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice,

verses.rationale: Renders negative oath force decisively without a misleading literal if; keeps repeated seeing.
verses.before: will see the land that I swore to their ancestors. None of people who despised me will see it.
verses.after: they will never see the land I swore to give their ancestors. None who despise me will see it.
verses.tsw_comparator: shall see the land that I swore to their ancestors. None of those who despised me shall see it.

verses.rationale: Keeps Caleb alone in this exception statement without adding Joshua from verse 30.
verses.before: But my servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit with him and followed me fully, I will bring into the land where he went, and his offspring will possess it.
verses.after: But my servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed me fully. I will bring him into the land he entered, and his descendants will possess it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But my servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit with him and followed me fully, I will bring into the land where he went, and his offspring shall possess it.

verses.rationale: Preserves valley, tomorrow and retreat direction; Sea of Reeds follows Hebrew yam suf with conventional name noted.
verses.before: Now the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valleys. Tomorrow turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.”
verses.after: The Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow, turn back and set out into the wilderness by the road toward the Sea of Reeds.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valleys. Tomorrow turn and set out for the wilderness by the way of the Red Sea.”

verses.rationale: Marks the new speech and both recipients without blending it with the earlier Moses-only dialogue.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,
verses.after: The LORD then spoke to Moses and Aaron:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the broken how-long outburst and repeated complaints rather than supplying a long explanatory clause.
verses.before: “How long will I bear with this evil congregation who grumble against me? I have heard the grumblings of the Israelites that they grumble against me.
verses.after: “How long—this evil community, complaining against me! I have heard the Israelites’ complaints against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “How long shall I bear with this evil congregation who grumble against me? I have heard the grumblings of the Israelites that they grumble against me.

verses.rationale: Keeps oath and ears image linking the punishment to their earlier death wish.
verses.before: Say to them: ‘As I live, says the LORD, just as you have spoken in my hearing, so I will do to you.
verses.after: Tell them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what you have said in my ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them: ‘As I live, says the LORD, just as you have spoken in my hearing, so I will do to you.

verses.rationale: Retains corpses, census scope and twenty-year threshold without extending the category to uncounted people.
verses.before: Your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness, all of you who were counted in the census, from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against me.
verses.after: Your corpses will fall in this wilderness—all of you who were counted, your full number from twenty years old and up, who complained against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness, all of you who were counted in the census, from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against me.

verses.rationale: Preserves raised-hand oath and both named exceptions; does not replace the oath image with abstraction.
verses.before: Not one of you will enter the land in which I lifted my hand to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.after: You will certainly not enter the land where I raised my hand and swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not one of you shall enter the land in which I lifted my hand to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

verses.rationale: Repeats little ones/plunder and retains know rather than promising an added degree of prosperity.
verses.before: But your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring in, and they will know the land that you rejected.
verses.after: But your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring in. They will know the land you rejected.
verses.tsw_comparator: But your little ones, whom you said would become plunder, I will bring in, and they shall know the land that you rejected.

verses.rationale: Keeps the blunt repeated corpse judgment; familiarity is no reason to remove repetition.
verses.before: But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.
verses.after: As for you, your corpses will fall in this wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for you, your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness.

verses.rationale: Retains shepherd life and prostitution metaphor for faithlessness; note distinguishes figurative accusation from an asserted sexual act.
verses.before: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness forty years and will bear your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
verses.after: Your children will live as shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the cost of your prostitution, until the last of your corpses lies in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your children shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years and shall bear your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Preserves doubled day/year correspondence and forty figures; difficult tenuah rendered opposition with alternatives noted.
verses.before: According to the number of the days in which you explored the land, forty days, a year for each day, you will bear your iniquities forty years, and you will know my opposition.’
verses.after: For the forty days you scouted the land, you will bear your wrongdoing for forty years—a year for each day, a year for each day. You will know my opposition.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the number of the days in which you explored the land, forty days, a year for each day, you shall bear your iniquities forty years, and you shall know my opposition.’

verses.rationale: Keeps divine self-identification, oath certainty, gathering-against and both death clauses.
verses.before: I, the LORD, have spoken. Surely I will do this to all this evil congregation gathered together against me. In this wilderness they will come to an end, and there they will die.”
verses.after: I, the LORD, have spoken. I will certainly do this to the whole evil community that has gathered against me. They will come to their end in this wilderness; there they will die.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: I, the LORD, have spoken. Surely I will do this to all this evil congregation gathered together against me. In this wilderness they shall come to an end, and there they shall die.”

verses.rationale: Follows read-form causative complaining while exact source binding includes both written/read forms.
verses.before: The men whom Moses sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing a bad report about the land—
verses.after: The men Moses had sent to scout the land came back and stirred the whole community to complain against him by spreading a bad report about the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men whom Moses sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing a bad report about the land—

verses.rationale: Retains repeated bad-report identification and plague as means, not a vague disappearance.
verses.before: those men who brought the bad report about the land died by a plague before the LORD.
verses.after: Those men who spread the bad report died by a plague before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: those men who brought the bad report about the land died by a plague before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Restricts survival contrast to the scouts, retaining both fathers and names.
verses.before: Yet Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive from those men who went to explore the land.
verses.after: Of the men who went to scout the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive from those men who went to explore the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves grief without declaring repentance or mocking the people’s response.
verses.before: Moses spoke these words to all the Israelites, and the people mourned greatly.
verses.after: When Moses told all this to the Israelites, the people mourned deeply.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses spoke these words to all the Israelites, and the people mourned greatly.

verses.rationale: Keeps early ascent, self-presentation and confession; no added claim that confession restores the earlier command.
verses.before: They rose early in the morning and went up toward the heights of the hill country, saying, “Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD spoke of, for we have sinned.”
verses.after: Early the next morning they went up toward the heights of the hill country. “Here we are!” they said. “We will go up to the place the LORD spoke of. We have sinned.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They rose early in the morning and went up toward the heights of the hill country, saying, “Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD spoke of, for we have sinned.”

verses.rationale: Uses direct contemporary question while retaining prediction of failure.
verses.before: Yet Moses said, “Why are you now crossing the command of the LORD? This will not succeed.
verses.after: But Moses said, “Why are you disobeying the LORD’s command? This will not succeed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Moses said, “Why are you now crossing the command of the LORD? This will not succeed.

verses.rationale: Retains prohibition, absence and defeat as linked reasons without diluting the danger.
verses.before: Do not go up, for the LORD is not in your midst, so that you may not be struck down before your enemies.
verses.after: Do not go up. The LORD is not among you, and your enemies will defeat you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not go up, for the LORD is not in your midst, so that you may not be struck down before your enemies.

verses.rationale: Preserves both peoples, sword death and turned-away explanation in Moses’ warning.
verses.before: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.”
verses.after: Amalekites and Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. You have turned away from following the LORD, so the LORD will not be with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you.”

verses.rationale: Renders reckless presumption, retaining the contrast with Moses and ark remaining; does not invent their motives.
verses.before: But they presumed to go up to the heights of the hill country, though the ark of the covenant of the LORD and Moses did not move from the midst of the camp.
verses.after: Still, they presumed to go up into the heights of the hill country. Neither Moses nor the ark of the LORD’s covenant left the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they presumed to go up to the heights of the hill country, though the ark of the covenant of the LORD and Moses did not move from the midst of the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserves both attack verbs and the extent to Hormah, without inventing a casualty count.
verses.before: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and beat them down as far as Hormah.
verses.after: The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, attacked them and battered them all the way to Hormah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and beat them down as far as Hormah.

verses.rationale: Marks the shift from narrative judgment to divine ritual instruction without inventing an explanation for its placement.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses these instructions:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains when rather than if and the promise of a place to live; sentence continues into offering conditions.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of your dwelling places that I am giving you,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you enter the land I am giving you to live in,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of your dwelling places that I am giving you,

verses.rationale: Keeps every occasion and animal grouping; offering by fire follows established ishsheh terminology, with the alternative food-offering understanding noted.
verses.before: and you make an offering by fire to the LORD, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow, as a freewill offering, or at your appointed festivals, to make a pleasing aroma to the LORD from the herd or flock,
verses.after: and you prepare an offering by fire for the LORD from the herd or flock—a burnt offering or a sacrifice to fulfill a vow, as a voluntary gift, or at your appointed festivals—to make a pleasing aroma for the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: and you make an offering by fire to the LORD, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow, as a freewill offering, or at your appointed festivals, to make a pleasing aroma to the LORD from the herd or flock,

verses.rationale: Makes implied ephah unit explicit and preserves exact flour/oil proportions.
verses.before: then the one presenting the offering will present to the LORD a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil.
verses.after: the person bringing the offering must also present to the LORD a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-quarter of a hin of oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the one presenting the offering shall present to the LORD a grain offering of one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil.

verses.rationale: Retains quarter-hin wine for each lamb and both sacrifice types.
verses.before: You will prepare one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice for each lamb.
verses.after: For each lamb, prepare one-quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall prepare one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the burnt offering or sacrifice for each lamb.

verses.rationale: Separates ram ration from lamb ration and retains both quantities.
verses.before: For a ram, prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,
verses.after: For a ram, prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a ram, prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil,

verses.rationale: Preserves ram wine measure and aroma phrase without collapsing into verse 6.
verses.before: and one-third of a hin of wine for a drink offering. You will present it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: Also present one-third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and one-third of a hin of wine for a drink offering. You shall present it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps bull, vow and well-being alternatives; uses the established offering name.
verses.before: When you prepare a bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD,
verses.after: When you prepare a bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: When you prepare a bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD,

verses.rationale: Retains bull’s larger flour/oil amounts and connection to the preceding condition.
verses.before: then with the bull will be presented a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
verses.after: bring with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: then with the bull shall be presented a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,

verses.rationale: Keeps half-hin wine and both fire/aroma classifications.
verses.before: and you will present half a hin of wine for a drink offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: Bring half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you shall present half a hin of wine for a drink offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves all animal categories, including goats, without conflating the rations.
verses.before: Thus it will be done for each bull, ram, male lamb, or young goat.
verses.after: Do this for each bull, each ram, and each lamb or young goat.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus it shall be done for each bull, ram, male lamb, or young goat.

verses.rationale: Makes multiplication per animal explicit rather than implying one ration per ceremony.
verses.before: According to the number you prepare, so you will do for each, according to their number.
verses.after: However many animals you prepare, do this for each one.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the number you prepare, so you shall do for each, according to their number.

verses.rationale: Retains native-born scope and recurring aroma language before the resident-foreigner extension.
verses.before: Every native-born Israelite will do these things in this way when presenting an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: Every native-born Israelite must follow these instructions when presenting an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when presenting an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses inclusive generic singular and preserves continuing residence and equal ritual obligation, not a modern citizenship category.
verses.before: If a resident alien lives with you, or whoever may be among you throughout your generations, and wishes to make an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, that person will do as you do.
verses.after: If a foreigner lives among you, now or in generations to come, and prepares an offering by fire with a pleasing aroma for the LORD, they must do as you do.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a resident alien lives with you, or whoever may be among you throughout your generations, and wishes to make an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, that person shall do as you do.

verses.rationale: Preserves one rule and explicit equal standing in this ritual context without expanding it into an unqualified modern political claim.
verses.before: As for the assembly, there will be one statute for you and for the resident alien who lives among you, a perpetual statute throughout your generations. As you are, so will the resident alien be before the LORD.
verses.after: The community must have one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you, a lasting rule throughout your generations. You and the foreigner stand alike before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the resident alien who lives among you, a perpetual statute throughout your generations. As you are, so shall the resident alien be before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both torah and mishpat, not one undifferentiated reference to law.
verses.before: One instruction and one ordinance will be for you and for the resident alien who lives among you.”
verses.after: You and the foreigner living among you must have the same instruction and the same ruling.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One instruction and one ordinance shall be for you and for the resident alien who lives among you.”

verses.rationale: Marks the next discrete divine instruction about the first dough.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD also instructed Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains bringing and arrival framing before the bread command.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When you come into the land where I am bringing you,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,

verses.rationale: Connects eating local bread and contribution without importing a percentage.
verses.before: and when you eat of the bread of the land, you will present a contribution to the LORD.
verses.after: and you eat the bread of that land, set aside a contribution for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: and when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall present a contribution to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains cake and first dough, with alternative coarse-meal sense noted, and the threshing-floor analogy.
verses.before: From the first of your dough you will present a loaf as a contribution; like a contribution from the threshing floor, so you will present it.
verses.after: Set aside a cake from the first of your dough as a contribution, just as you set aside a contribution from the threshing floor.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the first of your dough you shall present a loaf as a contribution; like a contribution from the threshing floor, so you shall present it.

verses.rationale: Preserves recurring first/dough wording and continuing obligation.
verses.before: From the first of your dough you will give to the LORD a contribution throughout your generations.
verses.after: Throughout your generations, give the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the first of your dough you shall give to the LORD a contribution throughout your generations.

verses.rationale: Preserves collective inadvertence and broad all-commands wording; does not narrow to idolatry without textual warrant.
verses.before: If you sin unintentionally and do not observe all these commandments that the LORD spoke to Moses—
verses.after: If you go astray unintentionally and fail to carry out all these commands that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
verses.tsw_comparator: If you sin unintentionally and do not observe all these commandments that the LORD spoke to Moses—

verses.rationale: Keeps the verse as an expansion of commands and the full temporal scope.
verses.before: everything the LORD commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave commandment and onward throughout your generations—
verses.after: everything the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command onward through your generations—
verses.tsw_comparator: everything the LORD commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave commandment and onward throughout your generations—

verses.rationale: Preserves unnoticed collective error, one bull versus one male goat, and distinct sacrificial functions.
verses.before: then if it was done unintentionally, without the knowledge of the congregation, the whole congregation will offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering.
verses.after: and this happens unintentionally, without the community’s knowledge, the whole community must prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma for the LORD, with its prescribed grain and drink offerings, and one male goat as a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: then if it was done unintentionally, without the knowledge of the congregation, the whole congregation shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Retains atonement and forgiveness with the stated grounds; no replacement with psychological language.
verses.before: The priest will make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, for it was unintentional and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
verses.after: The priest will make atonement for the whole Israelite community, and they will be forgiven. It was unintentional, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire for the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their error.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they shall be forgiven, for it was unintentional and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional sin.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit inclusion in forgiveness and collective inadvertence.
verses.before: The whole congregation of the Israelites will be forgiven, as well as the resident alien who lives among them, because all the people were involved in the unintentional sin.
verses.after: The whole Israelite community and the foreigner living among them will be forgiven, because all the people were involved in the unintentional error.
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole congregation of the Israelites shall be forgiven, as well as the resident alien who lives among them, because all the people were involved in the unintentional sin.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular person, female animal and age; generic human pronoun is inclusive.
verses.before: If one person sins unintentionally, that person will present a female goat a year old as a sin offering.
verses.after: If one person sins unintentionally, they must bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: If one person sins unintentionally, that person shall present a female goat a year old as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated atonement language and forgiveness without inventing an additional action.
verses.before: The priest will make atonement before the LORD for the person who sins unintentionally, when that person sins unintentionally, to make atonement, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: The priest will make atonement before the LORD for the person who sinned unintentionally. When atonement is made for them, they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who sins unintentionally, when that person sins unintentionally, to make atonement, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Keeps one instruction and both resident categories in the individual case.
verses.before: For the native-born among the Israelites and for the resident alien who lives among them, you will have one instruction for anyone who acts unintentionally.
verses.after: The same instruction applies to anyone who acts unintentionally, whether a native-born Israelite or a foreigner living among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the native-born among the Israelites and for the resident alien who lives among them, you shall have one instruction for anyone who acts unintentionally.

verses.rationale: Preserves raised-hand defiance and cut-off sanction with explanatory notes instead of silently specifying an execution procedure.
verses.before: But the person who acts with a high hand, whether native-born or resident alien, reviles the LORD; that person will be cut off from among the people.
verses.after: But anyone who acts with a raised hand, whether native-born or a foreigner, insults the LORD. That person must be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the person who acts with a high hand, whether native-born or resident alien, reviles the LORD; that person shall be cut off from among the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic cutting off and remaining guilt without softening to an administrative exclusion.
verses.before: Because that person has despised the word of the LORD and broken the commandment, that person will surely be cut off; their iniquity is upon them.”
verses.after: They have despised the LORD’s word and broken his command. That person must certainly be cut off; their guilt remains on them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Because that person has despised the word of the LORD and broken the commandment, that person shall surely be cut off; their iniquity is upon them.”

verses.rationale: Retains specific man, activity and Sabbath setting without assigning an unstated motive.
verses.before: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
verses.after: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath.
verses.tsw_comparator: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.

verses.rationale: Keeps discoverers as agents and all three recipients of the case.
verses.before: People who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation.
verses.after: Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron and the whole community.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation.

verses.rationale: Does not pretend the uncertainty was necessarily only the method of execution.
verses.before: They put him under guard, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
verses.after: They kept him in custody because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They put him under guard, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine attribution, death, community agency and location without explaining away the harm.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man will surely be put to death. The whole congregation will stone him with stones outside the camp.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses, “The man must be put to death. The whole community must stone him outside the camp.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man shall surely be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”

verses.rationale: Keeps enacted death and agency explicit; no euphemistic punishment summary.
verses.before: So the whole congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.after: The whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the whole congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.rationale: Retains the speech transition to tassels; clear shared wording may remain.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD said to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains tassels, garment corners and blue cord; no later knot-count custom imported.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations and to put a blue cord on the tassel at each corner.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord on each corner’s tassel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations and to put a blue cord on the tassel at each corner.

verses.rationale: Keeps tur link to scouts and sexual metaphor for unfaithfulness; avoids sanitizing the heart/eyes contrast.
verses.before: It will be a tassel for you to look at and remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, so that you do not follow after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you prostitute yourselves,
verses.after: These will be your tassels: when you look at them, remember all the LORD’s commands and carry them out. Do not go scouting after your own heart and eyes, prostituting yourselves by following them.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be a tassel for you to look at and remember all the commandments of the LORD and do them, so that you do not follow after your own heart and your own eyes, after which you prostitute yourselves,

verses.rationale: Retains memory-action-holiness movement and switch to first-person divine commands.
verses.before: so that you may remember and do all my commandments and be holy to your God.
verses.after: Then you will remember and carry out all my commands and be holy to your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may remember and do all my commandments and be holy to your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves both identity formulas and the stated exodus purpose rather than removing repetition.
verses.before: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
verses.after: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
