verses.rationale: Preserves next-day timing, Aaron/Levi identity and full botanical progression. Hebrew 17:23.
verses.before: On the next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony, and look—Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted. It had brought forth buds, produced blossoms, and borne ripe almonds.
verses.after: The next day Moses entered the tent of the testimony. Aaron’s staff, representing Levi’s house, had sprouted! It had put out buds, produced blossoms and ripened almonds.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony, and look—Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted. It had brought forth buds, produced blossoms, and borne ripe almonds.

verses.rationale: Retains public display and each leader’s retrieval; no added explanation of their emotional response. Hebrew 17:24.
verses.before: Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his staff.
verses.after: Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each leader took his staff.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his staff.

verses.rationale: Preserves sign, complaint cessation and death-prevention purpose; no invented later placement inside ark. Hebrew 17:25.
verses.before: The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back before the testimony to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may bring their grumblings against me to an end and they may not die.”
verses.after: The LORD told Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the testimony. Keep it there as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may end their complaints against me and they will not die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back before the testimony to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may bring their grumblings against me to an end and they may not die.”

verses.rationale: Conveys emphatic command-fulfillment without supplying new action beyond the staff instruction. Hebrew 17:26.
verses.before: Moses did so. As the LORD commanded him, so he did.
verses.after: Moses did exactly as the LORD commanded him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses did so. As the LORD commanded him, so he did.

verses.rationale: Retains three cries and repeated lost as frightened speech, not proof that all are already dead. Hebrew 17:27.
verses.before: The Israelites said to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost! We are all lost!
verses.after: The Israelites said to Moses, “We are dying! We are lost! All of us are lost!
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites said to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost! We are all lost!

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated approach and closing question that leads into chapter 18’s access distinctions. Hebrew 17:28.
verses.before: Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the LORD’s tabernacle, dies. Are we all to perish?”
verses.after: Anyone who comes near—who comes near the LORD’s tabernacle—dies. Must we all die?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the LORD’s tabernacle, dies. Are we all to perish?”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes broader ancestral-house sanctuary liability from Aaron-and-sons priesthood liability; retains bearing guilt with note.
verses.before: The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your ancestral house with you will bear the iniquity connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you will bear the iniquity connected with your priesthood.
verses.after: The LORD said to Aaron, “You, your sons and your ancestral house with you must bear responsibility for offenses against the sanctuary. You and your sons must bear responsibility for offenses against your priesthood.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your ancestral house with you shall bear the iniquity connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the iniquity connected with your priesthood.

verses.rationale: Retains Levi/join wordplay in vocabulary and differentiates assistants from Aaron’s sons.
verses.before: Bring near also your brothers of the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, so that they may join you and serve you while you and your sons with you are before the Tent of the Testimony.
verses.after: Bring your fellow Levites, your ancestral tribe, near with you, so they may join you and serve you while you and your sons serve before the tent of the testimony.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bring near also your brothers of the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, so that they may join you and serve you while you and your sons with you are before the Tent of the Testimony.

verses.rationale: Preserves limits despite Levitical service and shared lethal liability, not only a penalty on the intruder.
verses.before: They will keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, but they will not come near the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, so that neither they nor you die.
verses.after: They must attend to your duties and the duties of the whole tent. But they must not approach the sanctuary’s furnishings or the altar, or both they and you will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, but they shall not come near the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, so that neither they nor you die.

verses.rationale: Keeps joined service and restriction; unauthorized is a role category, not an ethnic foreigner.
verses.before: They will join you and keep charge of the Tent of Meeting for all the service of the tent, and no outsider will come near you.
verses.after: They are to join you and take care of the tent of meeting, doing all the work of the tent. No unauthorized person may approach you.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall join you and keep charge of the Tent of Meeting for all the service of the tent, and no outsider shall come near you.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct Aaronic responsibility and again linking preceding plague narrative.
verses.before: You will keep charge of the sanctuary and charge of the altar, so that wrath may no longer come upon the Israelites.
verses.after: You must attend to the sanctuary and the altar, so that wrath will not fall on the Israelites again.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall keep charge of the sanctuary and charge of the altar, so that wrath may no longer come upon the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult double gift direction: to priests for service, dedicated to LORD; does not silently change to from-LORD wording.
verses.before: Look, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to perform the service of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: I myself have taken your fellow Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD to do the work of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to perform the service of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves altar/inside-curtain scope, gift-service ambiguity in note and explicit execution sanction without generalizing unrestricted access.
verses.before: But you and your sons with you will keep your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain. You will serve. I give your priesthood as a service of gift. Any outsider who approaches will be put to death.”
verses.after: You and your sons must attend to your priesthood in everything concerning the altar and what lies inside the curtain. You must carry out that service. I give you the priesthood as a gift of service. Any unauthorized person who approaches must be put to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But you and your sons with you shall keep your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain. You shall serve. I give your priesthood as a service of gift. Any outsider who approaches shall be put to death.”

verses.rationale: Renders mishchah as allotted portion with anointing-linked alternate noted; preserves custody and gift dimensions.
verses.before: Then the LORD spoke to Aaron: “Look, I have given you charge of my contributions, all the holy gifts of the Israelites. I have given them to you and your sons as a portion by reason of the anointing, a perpetual due.
verses.after: The LORD told Aaron, “I have put you in charge of the contributions made to me. All the Israelites’ holy gifts I have given to you and your sons as your allotted portion, a lasting provision.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD spoke to Aaron: “Look, I have given you charge of my contributions, all the holy gifts of the Israelites. I have given them to you and your sons as a portion by reason of the anointing, a perpetual due.

verses.rationale: Preserves portion not burned, all three offering types and heightened holy classification with consistent terminology.
verses.before: This will be yours from the most holy things not burned by fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering that they render to me will be most holy for you and your sons.
verses.after: This will be yours from the most holy offerings, the part kept back from the fire: all their gifts to me from grain offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings. These are most holy for you and your sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: This shall be yours from the most holy things not burned by fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering that they render to me shall be most holy for you and your sons.

verses.rationale: Adopts as-most-holy construal rather than commanding meals in Holy of Holies; note records spatial alternate and priestly male scope.
verses.before: You will eat it as most holy; every male may eat it. It will be holy to you.
verses.after: Eat it as something most holy. Every male may eat it; you must treat it as holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall eat it as most holy; every male may eat it. It shall be holy to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit daughters and clean-household permission, contrasted with preceding male-only most-holy offerings.
verses.before: This also is yours: the contribution of their gifts, together with all the elevation offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual due. Everyone clean in your household may eat it.
verses.after: These are yours too: the contributions from their gifts, including all the Israelites’ wave offerings. I give them to you, your sons and your daughters with you as a lasting provision. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
verses.tsw_comparator: This also is yours: the contribution of their gifts, together with all the elevation offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual due. Everyone clean in your household may eat it.

verses.rationale: Renders fat idiom as finest, preserves new wine and grain without narrowing grain to wheat.
verses.before: All the best of the oil, all the best of the new wine and grain, the first of what they give to the LORD, I have given to you.
verses.after: I give you all the finest oil, all the finest new wine and grain—the first of these that they give to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the best of the oil, all the best of the new wine and grain, the first of what they give to the LORD, I have given to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps first ripeness, land produce and clean-household entitlement.
verses.before: The first ripe fruit of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will be yours. Everyone clean in your household may eat it.
verses.after: The first ripe produce of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD belongs to you. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first ripe fruit of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD shall be yours. Everyone clean in your household may eat it.

verses.rationale: Conveys herem as irrevocable dedication in this context, without making destruction its automatic meaning.
verses.before: Everything devoted in Israel will be yours.
verses.after: Everything in Israel devoted irrevocably to God belongs to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everything devoted in Israel shall be yours.

verses.rationale: Retains womb-opening image and mandatory redemption for humans and unclean animals; no human sacrifice implication.
verses.before: Every first issue of the womb from all flesh that they present to the LORD, whether human or animal, will be yours. Even so, you will surely redeem the firstborn human, and you will redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
verses.after: The first to open the womb among all flesh, human or animal, that they present to the LORD belongs to you. But you must redeem the firstborn humans, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every first issue of the womb from all flesh that they present to the LORD, whether human or animal, shall be yours. Nevertheless, you shall surely redeem the firstborn human, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.

verses.rationale: Keeps month threshold, five-shekel redemption and twenty-gerah standard without modern monetary equivalence.
verses.before: Their redemption price, from one month old, you will redeem according to your valuation, five shekels of silver according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
verses.after: For those who must be redeemed, from one month old, the redemption price is your valuation of five shekels of silver, using the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their redemption price, from one month old, you shall redeem according to your valuation, five shekels of silver according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

verses.rationale: Keeps three clean animal groups exempt from redemption and distinguishes blood splashing from fat burning.
verses.before: But the firstborn of an ox, the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat you will not redeem; they are holy. You will splash their blood against the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: But do not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep or goats; they are holy. Splash their blood against the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the firstborn of an ox, the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall splash their blood against the altar and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves meat entitlement, breast and specifically right thigh without vague generic portions.
verses.before: Their flesh will be yours, like the breast of the elevation offering and the right thigh; it will be yours.
verses.after: Their meat belongs to you, just as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh belong to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their flesh shall be yours, like the breast of the elevation offering and the right thigh; it shall be yours.

verses.rationale: Retains daughters again, lasting provision and concrete covenant-of-salt image rather than substituting an explanation.
verses.before: All the contributions of the holy things that the Israelites contribute to the LORD I have given to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual due. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD for you and your offspring with you.”
verses.after: I give all the contributions from the holy gifts that the Israelites set aside for the LORD to you, your sons and your daughters with you as a lasting provision. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your descendants with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the contributions of the holy things that the Israelites contribute to the LORD I have given to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual due. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD for you and your offspring with you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast between territorial share and LORD-as-inheritance, without denying later Levitical towns.
verses.before: The LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
verses.after: The LORD said to Aaron, “You will receive no inheritance in their land and have no share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Aaron, “You shall have no inheritance in their land, nor shall you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.

verses.rationale: Keeps all tithes, inheritance and compensation-for-service connection; no modern church finance rule added.
verses.before: “To the Levites, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance in return for the service they perform, the service of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: To the Levites I give every tithe in Israel as their inheritance in return for the service they perform, the work of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: “To the Levites, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance in return for the service they perform, the service of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains death consequence and general Israelite access boundary in contrast with authorized Levites.
verses.before: The Israelites will no longer approach the Tent of Meeting, bearing sin and dying.
verses.after: The Israelites must no longer approach the tent of meeting, incurring guilt and dying.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Israelites shall no longer approach the Tent of Meeting, bearing sin and dying.

verses.rationale: Keeps Levitical responsibility and no territorial inheritance; their offenses retains pronoun ambiguity with note.
verses.before: The Levites will perform the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they will bear their iniquity. It will be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, and among the Israelites they will have no inheritance.
verses.after: The Levites are to do the work of the tent of meeting and bear responsibility for their offenses. This is a lasting rule throughout your generations. They will receive no inheritance among the Israelites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites shall perform the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they shall bear their iniquity. It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, and among the Israelites they shall have no inheritance.

verses.rationale: Retains explanatory repetition and tithe as contribution, not a second land allotment.
verses.before: For the tithe of the Israelites, which they contribute to the LORD as a contribution, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. Therefore I have said concerning them, ‘Among the Israelites they will have no inheritance.’”
verses.after: I have given the Levites as their inheritance the Israelites’ tithes, which they set aside as a contribution for the LORD. That is why I have told them they will receive no inheritance among the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the tithe of the Israelites, which they contribute to the LORD as a contribution, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. Therefore I have said concerning them, ‘Among the Israelites they shall have no inheritance.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps change of recipient from Aaron to Moses for instructions addressed to Levites.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD gave Moses this instruction:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves tenth-of-tenth obligation without confusing it with the entire tithe.
verses.before: “Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you will contribute from it a contribution to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
verses.after: “Tell the Levites: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe I have given you as your inheritance, set aside a contribution from it for the LORD—a tithe of the tithe.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you shall contribute from it a contribution to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.

verses.rationale: Retains agricultural accounting analogy despite Levites not receiving a tribal land inheritance.
verses.before: Your contribution will be counted to you as if it were grain from the threshing floor and fullness from the winepress.
verses.after: Your contribution will be counted as though it were grain from the threshing floor or produce from the winepress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your contribution shall be counted to you as though it were grain from the threshing floor and fullness from the winepress.

verses.rationale: Keeps Levites as contributors and Aaron as recipient, not an unnamed public fund.
verses.before: Thus you also will contribute a contribution to the LORD from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites, and from it you will give the LORD’s contribution to Aaron the priest.
verses.after: So you too must set aside a contribution for the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites. Give this contribution for the LORD to Aaron the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you also shall contribute a contribution to the LORD from all your tithes that you receive from the Israelites, and from it you shall give the LORD’s contribution to Aaron the priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves full holy portion and finest quality, not leftovers after consumption.
verses.before: From all your gifts you will contribute every contribution due to the LORD, from all the best of them, the holy part from them.
verses.after: From every gift you receive, set aside the LORD’s full contribution, its holy portion from the finest of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: From all your gifts you shall contribute every contribution due to the LORD, from all the best of them, the holy part from them.

verses.rationale: Clarifies remainder implied by the contribution/remnant sequence while retaining both agricultural comparisons.
verses.before: So say to them: ‘When you have contributed the best of it, then the rest will be counted to the Levites as produce of the threshing floor and produce of the winepress.
verses.after: Tell them: When you have set aside the finest part, what remains will count for the Levites as produce from the threshing floor or the winepress.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore say to them: ‘When you have contributed the best of it, then the rest shall be counted to the Levites as produce of the threshing floor and produce of the winepress.

verses.rationale: Preserves household permission, unrestricted location for remainder and compensation rationale.
verses.before: You may eat it in any place, you and your households, for it is your wages in return for your service at the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: You and your households may eat it anywhere, because it is your payment for service at the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may eat it in any place, you and your households, for it is your wages in return for your service at the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional lack of guilt and final profanation/death warning, linking holiness and distribution rather than mere finances.
verses.before: You will bear no sin because of it when you contribute the best of it. You will not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, so that you do not die.’”
verses.after: You will incur no guilt on its account when you have set aside the finest part. Do not profane the Israelites’ holy gifts, and you will not die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall bear no sin because of it when you contribute the best of it. You shall not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, so that you do not die.’”
